Messages.Author: Ashur
Messages.Body:
First: Congratulations to the win!

Then, IMHO: This is possibly the most boring deck archetype ever to plague Vtes. I have no idea what the designer thought of when Una was created.

And as for playing it: why not just play solitaire, if you don´t want to interact with other players? "Oh, no one has a DI on hand? OK, then I just won the game. Nice of you others to drop by. Have a nice day!"

"My strategy? Luck is my strategy, of course."

Messages.Author: KevinM
Messages.Body:
> Ashur wrote:
> And as for playing it: why not just play solitaire, if you don´t want to interact with other players? "Oh, no one has a DI on hand? OK, then I just won the game. Nice of you others to drop by. Have a nice day!"
>
A single, or even multiple 'cancel' cards do not stop an Una deck, nor does a lack of 'cancel' cards allow an Una deck to instantly win.

There are many factors that force the deck into certain positions, and the deck is difficult to play well, even though it appears on the surface to be simple. Sure, you can get a fair amount of VPs with it, but putting yourself into a position to get the GW every table isn't easy. I've seen this to be true for almost all Tier1 decks, including Kindred Spirits decks.

Messages.Body:
> Ashur wrote:
> First: Congratulations to the win!
>
> Then, IMHO: This is possibly the most boring deck archetype ever to plague Vtes. I have no idea what the designer thought of when Una was created.
>
> And as for playing it: why not just play solitaire, if you don´t want to interact with other players? "Oh, no one has a DI on hand? OK, then I just won the game. Nice of you others to drop by. Have a nice day!"
>
I recommend playing this deck to understand why it's interesting and not solitaire. Yes, there are some games you'll win, but it generates a huge amount of table hate, and many things can go wrong.

In a game I suspect I'll remember forever, I was playing Euro Brujah and my prey was an Una deck. I was about to torpor Una with the 3rd or 4th 2nd tradition of the turn, when my grandpredator DI'd *my* 2nd Tradition. Una proceeded to hunt back up to full health, torpored her prey's minions (and mine), got 1 VP, and was done. My grandpredator won, without a predator to hassle him.

Una definitely is far from "auto-win unless there is a DI or Pentex."

Ira

Messages.Author: ICL
Messages.Body:
CCGs cater to a lot of different interests. Ideally, from a game management perspective, you provide different types of cards/strategies to cater to varying interests but limit those that annoy a large segment of the playerbase.

My greatest problem with Imbued isn't effectiveness or playing a different game or Events, it's how deadly dull I find them. I like cards in hand to be the most important thing in CCGs, not cards in play. Meanwhile, I'm well aware that others find Imbued interesting.

Take anything and some will find it interesting and others dull.

I find stealth bleed to be the most interesting strategy in the game. The battle of trying to deal damage through intercept and, more importantly, bounce interests me far more than any combo deck does. Yet, I routinely see comments to the effect that it's the most boring strategy in the game.

To each their own.

Traveller Card Game
